lesson.menu_desc: Take a position in the case discussion -- if + past, would -- 28 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 15 -- If You Were the CEO
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Mauricio | Lesson 15 -- If You Were the CEO

listenings.text: Welcome to the case method. In this room, I will not give you the answer. I will ask you a question, and the question is always the same: if you were the CEO, what would you do? There is no right answer, but there is a wrong one. The wrong answer is, it depends. Of course it depends. Everything depends. I want you to take a position. Say, if I were the CEO, I would close the factory, and then back it up with one number. If a classmate plays devil's advocate, good. Listen, and answer. If you changed your mind every time someone pushed back, you would never decide anything. And a CEO who never decides is not a CEO.

On my third day, the professor looked at me and asked, what would you do if you were the CEO of this airline? My gut feeling said, do not cut costs, protect the service. But I was afraid. So I said, it depends. The professor smiled and waited. So I tried again. I said, if I were the CEO, I would not cut costs this year. In the long run, the airline would lose its best clients. Then a classmate played devil's advocate. He said, but the airline is losing money now. I said, fair point, but the stakeholders who matter most are the clients. Nobody agreed with me. And that was fine. The professor wrote my name on the board.

defs: to say clearly what you think and what you would do
a person or group affected by a decision
after a long time, in the future
an idea that comes from instinct, not from numbers
a person who argues the other side, to test an idea
